answers.answer: With Docker running and the bot address open, choose Use the shared NomNomzBot app and Next on Twitch app. Choose Skip for Bot account, Spotify, Discord and YouTube. On the last card, skipped services may remain Not set and Event feed need not be healthy. Choose Finish setup, then sign in as the broadcaster to connect the channel.
quote: Have the Docker installation running and open the bot’s address in your browser.
For the quickest first sign-in, choose the shared Twitch app and skip the optional services.
Choose Use the shared NomNomzBot app, then Next.
This records your choice and completes the required Twitch step without filling in a Client ID or Client Secret.
Choose Skip to have your broadcaster account type the bot’s chat messages.
A separate bot account is optional.
Choose Skip on each optional service you do not need yet.
You can reach your first Twitch sign-in without creating any of these apps.
It is fine for skipped services to remain Not set.
Choose Finish setup.
The bot saves completion, closes the open key-changing window and opens the dashboard/sign-in flow.
Sign in as the broadcaster to connect your channel.

answers.answer: No separate bot account, Twitch Client Secret or healthy Event feed is needed for first sign-in. For an own app, the article says only Client ID is required and a secret optionally enables one-tap sign-in. UNKNOWN: whether registration can proceed with unverified Twitch email and two-factor authentication off, what must change, and where that requirement is established. The article gives a Developer Console link and registration steps but says nothing about those account prerequisites or a source establishing them.
quote: Choose Skip to have your broadcaster account type the bot’s chat messages.
A separate bot account is optional.
Only the Client ID is required.
A Client Secret is optional and adds one-tap sign-in; without it, sign-in uses a code.
A healthy event feed is not required for your first sign-in.
You also need the exact callback address shown by this bot’s setup card.
On Twitch app, open the Twitch Developer Console using the card’s link and register a new application.
Choose the Chat Bot category, create the app and copy its Client ID.

answers.answer: The bot saves setup completion, closes the open key-changing window and opens the dashboard/sign-in flow. Before completion anyone who can reach the address can change application keys. Afterward only a bot administrator can replace them; channel moderator access is insufficient.
quote: Choose Finish setup.
The bot saves completion, closes the open key-changing window and opens the dashboard/sign-in flow.
Until you choose Finish setup, anyone who can reach the bot’s address can change these application keys.
Afterward, changing them requires a bot administrator; being a channel moderator is not enough.

answers.answer: Yes, skip YouTube setup for YouTube song requests: their search and playback use a separate public/keyless path and need neither the Google app nor a YouTube account connection. No, saving Spotify app credentials alone does not link the account or select a playback device; both still need configuring afterward.
quote: YouTube song requests do not need the Google app or a YouTube account connection: music search and playback use a separate public/keyless path.
Saving Spotify app details prepares its account connection and music features; it does not link your account or choose a playback device.
These credentials identify an application; they do not finish linking an individual account.
Spotify still needs its account and playback device configured.
